card.heading: UNFINISHED MONUMENT
card.body: Work ceased in 1656 upon Mohammad Adil Shah's death, leaving elements unfinished.

card.heading: LOST INGENUITY?

verdict.myth_fields: none: no fact sheet in data/fact_sheets or data/script_library carries a cards.myths entry (refuting_fact_id appears in no JSON file in the repository). A real myth-vs-fact card cannot be rendered from existing inputs.
verdict.statement_fields: one: data/fact_sheets/hal_saflieni_hypogeum.json cards.statements S1, check verdict 'needs_check' with no runs and no signature, so card_fields.verify_field refuses it.
verdict.gated_titles: every run's fact_review holds only public_fingerprint / sheet_path / sheet_sha256 / review_rules_fingerprint, with no check record, so design_cards.gated_text refuses Gated('title'|'youtube_title') on every run (fact_evidence.checked_fact_review: no current check record).
verdict.consequence: Every hook, chapter and myth card needs a checked, signed card field. None exists. The real inputs are the fact sheets' facts, the runs' titles, act titles and hero photos below; the card fields themselves must be produced by fact_sheet.build + card_fields.check_cards (with a checker key) before a card can be rendered honestly. Anything rendered before that is new and must be labelled.

facts_naming_a_refuted_belief.statement: The legend that Damascus blades were quenched by thrusting them six times into the body of an enslaved person originated as a prank article published in the Chicago Tribune on November 4, 1894.

statements.text: UNESCO inscribed the Ħal Saflieni Hypogeum on the World Heritage List in 1980.

facts_naming_a_refuted_belief.statement: A medieval Marathi legend recounts that an architect named Kokasa carved the structure from the summit down so the queen could view the completed shikhara within a week's time.
Initially considered an extraterrestrial impact crater, the impact theory was disproved when suspected shock-metamorphism coesite was identified in 1969 as mislabeled barite.
